parsed.attack: The demand here is real but it is already fully absorbed at zero price: USCIS publishes the exact 100 civics questions, YouTube carries thousands of full mock naturalization interviews with millions of views, and community legal clinics and churches run free in-person mocks - so the applicant who is anxious already has somewhere to put the anxiety without paying. The N-400 review portion is an officer reading back answers the applicant themselves typed, against an approval rate above 90%, so the felt stakes are lower than the pitch assumes. The applicants who genuinely fear the interview are disproportionately the limited-English cohort who are least able to hold an unscripted spoken exchange with a simulated officer and least able to spend after a filing fee that already hurt; the applicants who can pay have usually retained an attorney who prepares them as part of the fee. The author's own kill metrics concede the shape of the problem - a one-shot life event yields under two credit packs and sub-$10 lifetime revenue against a $20-80 acquisition cost.
parsed.strongest_defence: Free mocks are one-directional video that cannot ask about your travel dates, cannot interrupt, and cannot go off-script, which is exactly the fear people report; the willingness to pay is already demonstrated by the attorneys and tutors charging $40-150 an hour for the same rehearsal, and the community-clinic channel converts distribution cost to near zero.
parsed.verdict_reason: The anxiety is genuinely felt and dated, but abundant free substitutes already satisfy it, so the paid behaviour - not the desire - is the unevidenced step.
